questions.question: A 100%-wide element overflows its parent. What is the likely cause?
questions.answer: It is using content-box, so padding and border are added outside the 100% content width. Set box-sizing: border-box globally or subtract the padding.

questions.question: Two stacked blocks have margin-bottom:24px and margin-top:16px. What is the gap?
questions.answer: 24px. Adjacent vertical margins collapse to the larger value, not the sum. Flex/grid gap does not collapse.

questions.question: Why doesn't z-index:9999 bring an element to the front?
questions.answer: It is inside a stacking context with lower precedence than a sibling context. z-index only orders within its own context, so raise the ancestor context or move the element.

questions.question: Why does position:sticky fail silently?
questions.answer: It needs an inset threshold (top/bottom/left/right), a scrolling ancestor, and room to move. An ancestor with overflow:hidden/auto or a fixed-height container prevents sticking.

questions.question: Why did em padding grow more than expected?
questions.answer: em is relative to the element's current font size and compounds through nesting. Use rem for spacing and type scales that should stay predictable.

questions.question: Difference between display:none and visibility:hidden?
questions.answer: display:none removes the box, layout space, accessibility, and interaction. visibility:hidden keeps layout space but removes paint, accessibility, and interaction.

questions.question: Why can't a span accept width and height?
questions.answer: Inline elements are sized by their content and line layout; width/height are ignored. Use inline-block, block, or make it a flex/grid item.

questions.question: Why is 100vh wrong on mobile?
questions.answer: 100vh uses the large viewport height, which includes area hidden by browser chrome, so content can be cut off. Use 100dvh (dynamic) or 100svh (smallest).
